findings.title: Duplicated tenant-name literal and untyped constant
findings.description: `CLOSED_BY: str = "runner"` repeats the literal `"runner"` that `RUNNER_TENANT_NAME: Final = "runner"` already defines at `tenant.py:30`. It is also annotated `str` instead of `Final`, unlike every other constant in the package. This breaks the project's "define a value once" rule. Define it once (for example in `faults.py` or a small shared constants module) and annotate it `Final`.

findings.title: `observe.py` is over the ~300-line guideline
findings.description: At 326 lines, `observe.py` is slightly past the project's file-size target. It holds two separable state machines: the confirmed-run path and the unconfirmed-launch path. Splitting the launch-confirmation logic into its own module would bring it within the guideline and make each path easier to read. This does not block the slice.

findings.title: Test module imports a private helper from another test module
findings.description: `test_budget_coverage.py` imports `_link` from `runner.test_probes` and needs a pyright suppression to do it. A test module depending on another test module's private helper is fragile, because a rename in `test_probes.py` breaks the budget-coverage test. Move `_link` into `tick_support.py`, which both tests already import from.

findings.title: Crash-entry test hooks use untyped monkeypatching
findings.description: `_hooked` returns `tuple[object, object]`, and `_arm_resolve_kill` replaces `Store.journal_resolve` with several `type: ignore` comments. The ignores are contained in a test-only process entry point and the result is correct. Typed `Callable` aliases (`PopenFactory` and the poll callable) would remove the need for the ignores. That would fit the requirement that strict pyright also covers test code.

findings.title: Process-boundary exception handling and store-failure propagation
findings.description: Store failures and `UpstreamShapeError` are re-raised so the process exits and recovery reconciles on restart. Anything else is logged with `logger.exception`, escalated, and isolated to the one project. `test_the_runner_package_has_exactly_one_broad_except` keeps this to a single catch. The expected external failures (`OSError` on log creation, `Popen` or `cf`, `TimeoutExpired`) are returned as values (`LaunchError`, `ProbeFailed`, `Fault`) with comments, not swallowed.

findings.title: Budgeted subprocess calls and the crash-ordering design
findings.description: The journal entry is written before `Popen`, and a block is written before the entry is resolved. Both steps are idempotent on re-entry (`_block_once`), and `test_crash_recovery.py` proves this with real SIGKILLs at four points. `TickBudget.allows_call` is checked before every poll, `cf` probe and launch, and `test_budget_coverage.py` enforces this with a guard on each call site.
